# Psalm 95 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Come let-us-sing-for-joy to-YHWH; let-us-shout to-rock-of our-salvation.

**2** Let-us-come-before his-face with-thanksgiving; with-songs let-us-shout to-him.

**3** For a-God great YHWH, and-a-King great above all gods.

**4** Who in-his-hand the-depths-of the-earth, and-peaks-of the-mountains to-him.

**5** Who to-him the-sea and-he made-it, and-the-dry-land his-hands formed.

**6** Come let-us-bow-down and-let-us-kneel; let-us-kneel before YHWH our-maker.

**7** For he our-God, and-we the-people-of his-pasture and-flock-of his-hand. Today if his-voice you-will-hear,

**8** 'Do-not harden your-heart as-at-Meribah, as-day-of Massah in-the-wilderness,

**9** When tested-me your-fathers, they-tried-me, also they-saw my-work.

**10** Forty years I-was-disgusted with-that-generation, and-I-said, "A-people erring-of heart they-are, and-they not have-known my-ways."

**11** So-I-swore in-my-anger, "If they-shall-enter into-my-rest!"'

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **95:7b-11**: Abrupt shift from worship invitation to divine warning — God's voice breaks in with the Meribah/Massah memory.

- **95:11**: 'If they-shall-enter' — an oath formula; the 'if' means 'they shall certainly NOT enter.' God's rest was forfeited by disobedience.

— EMET
